article: Women's event at the 43rd Chess Olympiad
statement: In this position, Mammadzada made a blunder by playing 106. Kh4? (106. Kh2 would have saved the game) and resigned immediately after 106... Kf3.
verdict: The diagram is the game position, but it is already lost: 106.Kh2 loses as well. The losing move was 105.Kg3 (105.Kh2 was the only drawing move).

article: Open event at the 44th Chess Olympiad
statement: In this position, Meier lost defensive coordination by playing 78... Qe3+?. Instead, 78... Qc7!! would have held despite being two pawns down. (diagram: White Kg5, Qf5, pawns g4, h5; Black Kh8, Qc5)
verdict: The diagram has the h-pawn on h5; in the game it stood on h6. With the pawn on h5 every Black move loses, 78...Qc7 included; with the pawn on h6 (the game) 78...Qc7 is the only drawing move, as the caption says.

statement: In this position Black is able to draw because his bishop is on the right color: 1... Be2 2. Kf4 Bc4 3. Kg5 Bd5! 4. Rc7 Ba2! 5. Kg6 Bb1+! 6. Kh6 Ba2! 7. Ra7 Bc4 and there is no way for White to make progress.
verdict: 1...Be2 loses; only 1...Ba2 and 1...Kg8 draw. The reply 2.Kf4 gives the draw back. The article 'Fortress (chess)' prints the same line from the same source with 1...Ba2, so Be2 is a misprint for Ba2.

statement: Spielt Weiß hier 1. Ke2–d2+? (analog 1. Ke2–f2+?), so hält Schwarz mit 1. … Ke5–f4 (bzw. Ke5–d4) remis. Richtig ist 1. Ke2–e3!
verdict: Black does not hold a draw: after 1.Kd2+ Kf4 or 1.Kf2+ Kd4 White still wins, in each case only by going back with 2.Ke2. The two checks lose time, not the win. In the diagram eight first moves keep the win; 1.Ke3 is the fastest.

statement: Weiß am Zug gewinnt mit 1. Sh6–g7+! Sf5xg7 2. h5–h6! (diagram: White Kh1, Ne6, pawn h5; Black Ke8, Nf5)
verdict: There is no knight on h6; the knight stands on e6 and the only winning move is 1.Ne6-g7+. 'Sh6' is a misprint for 'Se6'.

article: Endspiel König und Bauer gegen König und Bauer
statement: 1. … Kf7 2. Kd6! ebenfalls der einzige Gewinnzug
verdict: 2.Kd5 also wins (it loses time only), so 2.Kd6 is not the only winning move in the tablebase sense.

statement: Ignace Vandecasteele, 1233 Schakend Nederland 11/1970. Weiß zieht und gewinnt. Lösung: 1. Sf4 Kg5 2. Le3 Sa2 3. Kb3 d4 4. Se6+ Kf5 5. Sxd4+ Ke4 6. Sc2 ... (diagram: White Ka4, Bb6, Ng6; Black Kh6, Nc1, pawns d5, h7)
verdict: The diagrammed position is a draw. The printed line holds the draw up to 4.Ne6+, and then 4...Kg4 (instead of 4...Kf5) is the only move that keeps it.
